suites.name: test:repository-service
checkNames: identities: node SHA-256 equals the Site SHA-256 and revision identity follows the packet contract
manifest stream: identical to JSON.parse at hostile chunk boundaries, artefact arrays skipped, raw SHA-256 recorded
segmentation: front matter, fenced hashes, setext/AsciiDoc/RST headings; exact line ranges with CR and BOM kept
baseline build: policy gating, verified bytes, retrieval decisions, no notices before the baseline
search: ranked passages, phrases, prefixes, filters, two per file, and hostile query text never reaches FTS syntax
exact originals: BOM and CRLF preserved so the Site hash matches; refused with a reason when not retrievable
resumable build: a crashed job resumes after its last completed connector; store identity never changes
HTTP service: loopback host, bearer token and no browser origin; bounded JSON routes
Site retrieval through the corpus transport: same origin and identity as a GitHub read, re-verified, idempotent
candidate packet: accepted unchanged by the Site packet validator; locators carry exact knowledge.fetch commands
refresh after the baseline: successors, same-content commits, removals and withdrawals become contiguous notices
signed notices: verified by the Site with a notices-only key, applied to withdraw the invalidated project source

suites.name: test:repository-acquire
checkNames: path policy: allowed globs admit, denied globs win
dry run: the moved branch is resolved and the refresh planned without writing anything
fails closed: a truncated tree, a redirect and bytes that do not match the tree write nothing
acquisition: changed and new files downloaded and verified, unchanged reused, credentials quarantined without bytes
refresh: the new snapshot becomes successor revisions and notices; exact originals come from the new snapshot

suites.name: test:knowledge-repository
checkNames: discovery routes: status, ranked search and verified passages; never offered for unregistered or metadata-only files
retrieval and interpretation: the exact original through /api/commands, then a claim on the same line range
automatic revocation: a changed original becomes a signed invalidation, verified and applied when the project is read
Sources rendering: the connected repository surface, its receipts and actions; offline locators folded away

suites.name: test:brain-ahead
checkNames: SDD: the architecture reasoning record carries the vitals, product choices, Sol’s advice with outcomes and what the project learned
the reasoning record escapes table and list text, and stays inert in the HTML SDD
Mind Factory from the desk: each product with its documented mechanisms and the governed claims that name it
the comparison renders in Mind Factory, opened by the desk’s public entry point
Sol at a switch point: recall anchors on the Chapter 7 realisation; leads are worded from what Sol reads

suites.name: test:sol-evaluation
checkNames: every held-out case builds its packet from a real reference design and runs the full reasoning path
the teaching-domain capacity drafts expose advice that takes the Playbook example objective at face value
injected faults are caught: guards withhold invented numbers, guarantees, missing citations and out-of-bounds refinements
the metrics catch what the guards let through: a wrong verdict and advice missing its expected support
false-support proxy: numbers not in the cited sources and overclaiming words are flagged
adoption rates come from what architects did with advice in a real project, not from this harness

suites.output: PASS signed project release, independent authenticated review, exact source binding, scope, origin, replay, tamper, invalidation and Brain withdrawal. Inputs are synthetic; no real repository claim was approved.

suites.name: test:knowledge-second-brain

cleanInstall.note: Installs the lockfile's development tools (drizzle-kit, drizzle-orm) from the local npm cache without contacting the network, which proves the lockfile agrees with package.json. The runtime and the suites need no installed dependency.

failures.name: test:desk-browser
failures.classification: pre-existing test race (present in the supplied v19); fixed in the suite, assertions unchanged
failures.reason: After a drafted fix is applied, the desk's flash stays until the next one replaces it. The suite waited for any .dk-flash and read it 300 ms later, so a slower 12-command change review was read as the previous flash (line 220), or, when the first apply took longer than 8 s, the wait timed out (line 205). The supplied v19, run alone from its verified archive on this laptop, fails at the same assertion with the same text. The suite now waits up to 20 s for the flash that reports each action and notes the cell's pulse at the same moment; v19 and v20 then both pass all 16 checks.

dataset.title: Held-out decisions for evaluating Sol's advice
dataset.authority: Implementation-authored expectations. They were written from the designs' own readings before Sol was run on these cases, and none of these cases was used to write Sol's instructions, the guards or the provider test double. They are not independent expert review: an architect should review and amend them before any result is relied on.

limitations: Test double: the answers are canned. This run verifies the path, the guards and the metrics, not the quality of advice.
Expectations are implementation-authored and need independent architect review.
Metrics are automated proxies: they detect grounding and structural failures and disagreement with the expected class of advice, not the quality of architectural judgement.
The designs are reference and teaching examples, not a production system.

securityAndIntegrity.what: Loopback bind, bearer token, Host check, browser Origin refused; search input cannot inject FTS syntax.
The Site verifies and applies notices signed with a notices-only key, and that key cannot make a release receipt verify.
Signed release, independent authenticated review, exact source binding, scope, origin, replay, tamper, invalidation and Brain withdrawal.
Quarantined and metadata-only text is never searchable; excerpts are re-verified against the original on every request; the store keeps no second copy of third-party text.
Blob-verified downloads, credential quarantine, fail-closed truncation, redirects and tampering, and an untouched original root (loopback fake; no network).
No private keys, provider, GitHub, AWS or Slack tokens; no .env, databases, key material, repository store or corpus files; no personal data.
Every documentation revision verified against its manifest hash; catalogue checked against SHA256SUMS; zero unavailable, zero build errors.
